::: {.status}
The code is on [GitHub](https://github.com/NavyBlueCheese/pairs-trading-backtest).
:::

A classic pairs-trading strategy in Python, tested on daily Yahoo
Finance data for six stocks in three natural pairs: KO/PEP, XOM/CVX, and
JPM/BAC.

Pairs are chosen by cointegration, not correlation. Two stocks can be
highly correlated day to day and still drift apart forever; cointegration
means some combination of them is stationary, which is what makes betting
on the spread coming back reasonable. The test is Engle–Granger: regress
one log price on the other, then run an ADF test on the residuals.

**Avoiding the usual backtest traps:**

- The data is split 60/40 by time. Pair selection and the hedge ratio use
  only the first 60%, and the backtest runs only on the last 40%.
- The z-score's rolling mean and standard deviation (60 days) are lagged
  one bar, so a day's spread never appears in its own normalisation.
- Signals at the close of day *t* are filled at the open of *t+1*.
- Costs are 0.1% per leg, 0.4% per round trip.

**Trading rules:** enter when the z-score passes ±2, exit when it comes
back inside ±0.5, stop out beyond ±3.5, and close anything still open
after 30 days. The output reports total return, Sharpe ratio, maximum
drawdown, and win rate, along with the equity curve and a trade log.
